gap: No result ChatGPT got states that the Yaber T2 Plus, its pick for watching where there is no outlet, turns its brightness setting down from 100 to 60 when running on battery, so its brightness rating and its roughly 2.5-hour battery figure do not apply at the same time.
standout_why: I tried to read the cited rival pages but got little from them. RTINGS returned only navigation with no picks or figures. What Hi-Fi came back cut off. Travel + Leisure blocked the fetch, and the cited Costco JMGO PicoPlay+ page returned HTTP 429. So I could not confirm what those pages say about brightness on battery. Of the answers the shopper saw, the 11-12 Nov chat that picked the Yaber says only 'built-in battery rated for approximately 2.5 hours', and the 11-13 Nov chat that pointed to the XGIMI MoGo 4 says 'up to 2.5 hours of playback'. Neither says brightness drops on battery or which brightness rating applies. Our own current page lists the T2 Plus as '350 ISO lm' and 'About 2.5 h' in separate cells, with nothing linking them. The score is 2, not 3, because I could not rule out that the cited rival pages mention the drop.
decides: This confirms that for a battery-powered screen setup, the battery column cannot be read alongside the brightness column. The T2 Plus runs at a reduced brightness setting (60 of 100) on battery. Its brightness also appears as 450 ANSI lumens in reviews but as 350 ISO lumens on Yaber's own listing (this listing figure is from search output; I could not reopen the page). The page should footnote that battery hours are at reduced brightness. For outdoor screens of 100 to 120 inches, plug-in models with higher ratings (Aurzen EAZZE D1 MAX at 1,000 ANSI lumens; Vankyo H500R at 330 ANSI lumens) are the better pick when an outlet or power station is available. Battery models are the pick only when there is no power at all.

findings.label: Brightness setting on battery
findings.value: Drops from 100 to 60 in battery mode
findings.source_title: Yaber T2 Plus Projector Review: Cut The Cord For Smart Outdoor Movies (SlashGear, Steve Smith)
findings.note: Steve Smith, SlashGear: 'the brightness lowers from 100 to 60 in battery mode.' This is the projector's brightness setting, not a lumen measurement. Do not convert it to lumens (60% of 350 or 450), because light output is not proportional to the setting. Page shows 'Updated: Aug. 28, 2025'.

findings.label: Brightness as stated in the review
findings.source_title: Yaber T2 Plus Projector Review: Cut The Cord For Smart Outdoor Movies (SlashGear, Steve Smith)
findings.note: SlashGear states 'a max of 450 ANSI Lumens'. Our current page (read 2026-11-06) gives the maker spec table as 350 ISO lumens, and search output for Yaber's own listing and B&H also showed 350 ISO, which Yaber says was tested 'in the performance mode/high power mode'. I could not reopen those pages today (HTTP 429 and 403). The footnote: the 450 figure that reviewers repeat is not the maker's current 350 ISO rating, and neither number applies on battery.

findings.label: Battery runtime (rated)
findings.source_title: Yaber T2 Plus Projector Review: Cut The Cord For Smart Outdoor Movies (SlashGear, Steve Smith)
findings.note: The review repeats the rated '2.5 hours of video runtime' and gives no runtime of its own. Per the finding above, this runtime is at the reduced battery-mode brightness.
